title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: simplicial k-modules and derived functors in the Dold–Puppe sense. The dot over Λ stands for the exterior power index i (Λ^i). (–)^! seems to denote the associated chain complex (normalized or Moore complex) or its class in the derived category. P_• is a contractible simplicial k-module that is free in each degree. h_• ⊂ P_• is a degreewise rank-one sub-module, homotopically the constant k. The quotient Ψ_• = P_•/h_• is then a model of K(k,1), i.e. Ψ^! ≃ k[1].

The assertion to prove is that Λ^iΨ_• is a K(k,i). In derived-functor language Grothendieck rewrites this as (LΛ^i)(k[1]) ≃ k[i] (he writes k[-i], cohomological convention). He asks ('est-ce vrai?') whether, more generally, LΛ^i(L_•) ≃ Λ^i(L_•) for degreewise projective L_•. That is the standard Dold–Puppe fact that degreewise application computes the left derived functor on degreewise projective simplicial modules.

Proof via the filtration of P:
- From 0→h→P→Ψ→0 with h of rank one, one gets 0→Λ^{i-1}Ψ⊗h→Λ^iP→Λ^iΨ→0.
- Λ^iP is contractible ('flasque' here seems to mean acyclic or contractible), because Λ^i applied degreewise preserves simplicial homotopy equivalences.
- The homotopy long exact sequence then gives π_j(Λ^iΨ) ≅ π_{j-1}(Λ^{i-1}Ψ⊗h) ≅ π_{j-1}(Λ^{i-1}Ψ).
- Induction gives Λ^iΨ ≃ K(k,i).

NB a): probably (Λ^iΨ)^! ≃ k[i], i.e. k placed in degree i.

NB b): the same arguments would give other (less 'economical') models of K(k,i) built from Γ^i, Sym^i and tensor powers of Ψ.

Cor. 1.4: for a simplicial k-module A_•, π_n(A⊗Λ^iΨ) ≅ π_{n-i}(A). More precisely A⊗Λ^iΨ ≃ Σ^iA, the 'additive suspension'.

Purpose: in the 1976 IHÉS lectures on the divided-power de Rham complex, this supplies a small, functorial model of K(k,i) and of the i-fold suspension, presumably for comparing exterior, divided and symmetric powers of complexes. This is the décalage phenomenon. The neighbouring pages are typescript from SGA 7 IX (Néron models, monodromy) and are unrelated; the archive folder bundles material together.
errors: Sign/indexing convention: Λ^i(k[1]) is written k[-i] while NB a) says k[i] (k in degree i). This is a homological vs cohomological convention issue, not a mathematical error.

NB b) as written is doubtful. Sym^i(K(k,1)) is not a K(k,i) for i≥2: by décalage LSym^i(M[1]) ≃ LΛ^i(M)[i], which vanishes for M=k, i≥2. LΓ^i(k[1]) is also not concentrated in one degree. Tensor powers Ψ^{⊗i} ≃ k[i] (Eilenberg–Zilber) do work. Either the transcription/reading of b) is garbled, or the remark is mistaken for Sym^i and Γ^i.

The proof tacitly needs h_• to be degreewise free of rank one (for the Λ^{i-1}Ψ⊗h filtration) and homotopically equivalent to constant k (for the π_{j-1} identification). Neither is stated on the page.
The general claim LΛ^i(L_•) ≃ Λ^i(L_•) should be about simplicial modules. Applied naively to chain complexes, a degreewise Λ^i does not make sense; Dold–Kan is needed.

ideas.what: Degreewise exterior power of a degreewise projective simplicial module computes the left derived functor
ideas.modern_name: Dold–Puppe derived functors of non-additive functors

ideas.what: Λ^i of a simplicial model of K(k,1) is a K(k,i); LΛ^i(k[1]) ≃ k[i]
ideas.usually_credited_to: Bousfield, Quillen, Illusie (Complexe cotangent I, ch. I, 4.3)

ideas.what: Proof by the filtration of Λ^i of a contractible module and the homotopy long exact sequence
ideas.modern_name: Koszul-type filtration of exterior powers of an extension

ideas.what: A⊗Λ^iΨ ≃ Σ^iA as a model of i-fold additive suspension

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but standard derivation of the décalage of exterior powers, which is already in Illusie and Quillen. Its only interest is as evidence that Grothendieck worked through simplicial models for the divided-power de Rham lectures. Nothing new.
transcription_corrections: 'On peut aussi noter par la filtration' should probably read 'On peut aussi raisonner par la filtration'.
'(LΛ̇)(k[1]) ≃ Λ̇ k[1] = k[-i]': the dot denotes the exterior power index i, so read Λ^i.
'en ne avait' is likely 'en notant' or 'vu' (illegible); the sense is 'd'où la conclusion, via la suite exacte d'homotopie'.
Next to Λ^iP_* the margin says 'flasque' (i.e. acyclic or contractible). The crossed-out line was the attempted chain-complex version with (–)^!.
NB b) reads roughly 'Γ^i(⊗Ψ*) et Sym^i(Ψ*) (⊗Ψ*) ... K(k,i)'; the reading is uncertain.
Cor. 1.4: π_n(A_*⊗Λ^iΨ_*) ≃ π_{n-i}(A_*); bracket: 'on doit avoir A_*⊗Λ^iΨ_* ≃ Σ^iA_*, où Susp est la "suspension additive"'.
